clue.text: Central heating provides as occupational opening

definitions.meaning: central heating keeps a home warm, read literally as warming a dwelling
a party opening a newly occupied home

explanation.surface: A remark that a heating system is a fine opening line for a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: A party marking the move into new premises celebrates their first occupation, and heating literally does the warming of the home.

clue.text: Night so suited for entertaining

indicators.note: suited as in dressed up or fitted out, so the letters are put into a new outfit

explanation.surface: An evening in which everyone was well dressed for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' rearranges the seven letters of NIGHT SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining guests is acting as host to them; both are present participles.

clue.text: One upper class twit

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class usage
a nit is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a single posh idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item or the number one is a whole entity of one.

clue.text: Blow up a crazy general

indicators.note: crazy means wild or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mad army officer about to lose his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Story of a nobleman who joined Air Force ranks

indicators.note: the nobleman is said to join on to the ranks, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest rank in the RAF
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: The tale of an aristocrat who enlisted in the RAF as a humble airman.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is short for aircraftman, the lowest rank in Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative or report of events, a synonym of a tale.

clue.text: Ponder the end of Kintyre

definitions.meaning: the ... of Kintyre is the headland at the tip of the Kintyre peninsula in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The Mull of Kintyre is the southern tip of a long Scottish peninsula, famous from a pop song; a mull is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: To mull over is to consider at length, and a mull is a Scottish word for a promontory.

clue.text: Conjuring up rain by witchcraft in Africa

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
conjuring up suggests magic transforming the word rain into a new arrangement

parts.note: obi (obeah) is a form of Caribbean sorcery

explanation.surface: A witch doctor summoning a rainstorm somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjuring up' rearranges RAIN into NAIR, placed 'by' OBI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kenyan capital is a city on that continent, so the phrase locates it as a place there.

clue.text: Well placed to be an artist's model

definitions.meaning: in a comfortable or advantageous position
a model sits for a painter, ideally looking attractive

explanation.surface: Someone lucky enough to pose for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a fortunate position, while literally a model is posing and looking lovely.

clue.text: Army upset timber managers. Obviously!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the army's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
the heads of a logging firm, read as a compound of logger and heads

explanation.surface: Soldiers have annoyed the bosses of a forestry company, leaving everyone quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force; 'upset' turns it to AT. The whole clue describes the quarrel that results.
explanation.definitionFit: If soldiers upset forestry bosses, the two sides are naturally in dispute, which is what the idiom means.

clue.text: Not yet out to introduce ideas

annotationWithheld.why: Not yet out to introduce ideas: the wordplay reads 'Not yet out' as STILL IN, giving IN STILL only if 'Not ... out' (IN) is split around 'yet'; no contiguous parse exists
annotationWithheld.clue: Not yet out to introduce ideas

clue.text: Fellow on a fiddle is the first to join undercover group

parts.note: a cell is a small secret group of agents or terrorists

indicators.note: the first letter of the word to is taken

explanation.surface: A man running a scam is the first to join a secret organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow on a fiddle' suggests a swindler; the fiddle is a playful name for the instrument. 'join' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the cello is a person who plays a large bowed instrument, playfully called a fiddle.

clue.text: It could cause the downfall of an acid-head

definitions.text: It could cause the downfall of an acid-head

parts.words: It could cause the downfall of an acid-head
parts.note: a stumble that makes someone fall, and also an LSD user's hallucinatory experience

explanation.definitionFit: A stumble causes a fall, and a drug-induced high is what an LSD taker experiences.

clue.text: Complaint when the Right is discovered in a putsch

indicators.note: the right is found inside the putsch, so its letter goes within

parts.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Grumbling when right-wingers are found to be behind an attempted takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: The childhood throat illness is a medical ailment, a sense of complaint.

clue.text: Tropical palm found in two counties

indicators.note: two means the abbreviation appears twice in a row

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for county

explanation.surface: A palm tree growing in a pair of shires.
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut tree is a palm of the tropics.

clue.text: Treated to a drink while on one's feet

definitions.meaning: to stand someone a drink is to buy them one

explanation.surface: Being bought a drink while standing at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of stand covers both buying a round and having been upright.

clue.text: Mark and Anna's meal for the wandering Jew

parts.note: the name taken as written, without the possessive

explanation.surface: Two people providing food for a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: In Exodus the Israelites, wandering in the desert, were fed bread from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: The miraculous bread sustained the Israelites during their desert wanderings.

clue.text: Close neck-band worn by retiring woman

definitions.note: a phrase describing a garment, standing for the noun

parts.note: nigh means near
a tie is a band worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A tight collar on a shy lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here means going to bed, and the short gown is sleepwear for women.

clue.text: Rushing along to a circle of drinkers

parts.note: read as tea drinkers, the drink giving the letters
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Hurrying over to join a group out for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing along means moving at great speed.

clue.text: The sweet sentimentality of modern music?

indicators.note: the corn is that of pop, so pop comes first

parts.note: pop is popular music
corn is trite or mawkish material

explanation.surface: A grumble that today's songs are syrupy and over-sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugared puffed maize is a confection.

clue.text: Upset new fellow-that's sarcastic

parts.note: the word up turned over in a down entry reads bottom to top
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A newcomer who is offended by a biting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' supplies UP turned upside down, which in a down clue reads PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharp and caustic, like cutting wit.

clue.text: Not vintage stuff in the Isle of Wight

definitions.note: a phrase naming a place there, standing for the town

parts.note: new is the opposite of aged or vintage
the stuff here is port, a fortified wine often sold as vintage

explanation.surface: Cheap young wine being served on an island resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England; its county town shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is the island's administrative capital.

clue.text: A number travelling with cartographical aid

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on tour means travelling around

explanation.surface: A touring party carrying a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines joining points of equal height are a feature of maps.

clue.text: Honest assurance that there is time to visit Abraham's birthplace

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun of frankness

parts.note: I can is a promise that something is possible
to do a place is to visit it as a tourist
Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's home city in Genesis

explanation.surface: Being told truthfully that there is time to fit in a trip to Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN DO reads as an assurance that a visit is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness is the quality of being open and truthful.

clue.text: Professional man of vision

parts.note: suggests a visionary, but means an expert who treats eyesight

explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist is a professional concerned with eyesight.

clue.text: One's been mixed up for ages

definitions.note: the period is read as long ages

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the word with its s taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has been confused for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'One's' counts as a letter here because it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immensely long periods, as is a very long time.

clue.text: A lot of squadrons inspiring respect

parts.note: a wing is an air-force unit made up of several squadrons

explanation.surface: A large air formation that commands admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing means filling with wonder, a near synonym of inspiring respect.

clue.text: Hessian who once invaded Kent

definitions.meaning: a coarse sacking fabric made from plant fibre
Germanic invaders who settled Kent in the fifth century

explanation.definitionFit: The fibre is woven into sacking, and the tribe from Jutland settled in Kent after Rome left.

clue.text: Government hand-out from Republican senator

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain being on the dole means receiving unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemployment benefit is welfare money paid out, and the Kansas politician shared the surname.

clue.text: Nevertheless one may live in the Himalayas

definitions.note: a phrase describing the creature, standing for the noun

parts.note: yet means however
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Despite everything, someone might settle high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a legendary beast said to roam the mountains of Nepal and Tibet.

clue.text: Lot more fluctuation in pitch

indicators.note: fluctuation means wavering back and forth, so the letters shift around

explanation.surface: A singer's voice wobbling more and more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuation' rearranges LOT MORE, and the whole clue describes the musical effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical effect is a rapid wavering of a note.

clue.text: Somebody has to care for unanimity

parts.note: one means a person
to mind is to look after

explanation.surface: Someone has to look after the agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of a single opinion is complete agreement.

clue.text: One who draws people out

parts.note: suggests a coaxer of shy people, but means someone who sketches passers-by outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: A pavement painter draws portraits in public places outdoors.
